about: Ground plan for the Picasso area (docs/SMOOTH_PATHS.md, drawn by src/ground-plan.ts, checked by scripts/check_ground_plan.py). World metres: x east, z south. So far the car park's north entrance (its asphalt, the gatehouse island and the narrow planter) and, south of the car park, the service road's pavement and asphalt apron (data/picasso_service_frontage.json).
trust: The north entrance is traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot registered to the aerial (about 1.5 m) and read against Street View from Calle Loira and Calle Bolivia (Oct 2024) and IMG_3131. The apron's road-side edges follow the mapped Loira and Bolivia ribbons.

surfaces.name: Car park north entrance: asphalt round the gatehouse island
surfaces.note: Both lanes either side of the gatehouse island and the strip west of the narrow planter are asphalt in the photos (IMG_3131, Street View) and the Google view, joining Calle Loira and Calle Bolivia to the car park. Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the Esri aerial at 0.0385 m per pixel with the long wall's north end on (-91.4, -67.8), good to about 1.5 m. Its north edge runs just under the road ribbons; its south edge is the car-park outline's north edge, its east edge the long wall's inner face, its west edge the brick strip's east edge. The model drew this as generic terracotta before. The gatehouse island and the narrow planter are cut out of it and stand raised in the holes.

surfaces.name: Gatehouse island: terracotta apron on a white kerb
surfaces.note: The island between the entry and exit lanes: a round lawn bed to the north, the gatehouse in the middle and a terracotta apron to the south and east, where both barrier cabinets stand. White kerbs in Street View from Calle Loira. Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the Esri aerial at 0.0385 m per pixel with the long wall's north end on (-91.4, -67.8), good to about 1.5 m. The apron stands at the kerb top, about 0.15 m above the asphalt.

edges.note: White kerb round the island, standing about 0.15 m on the asphalt (Street View from Calle Loira and Calle Bolivia); its height is a guess.

surfaces.name: Gatehouse island: round lawn bed
surfaces.note: Lawn round the gatehouse's north and west sides under trees and palms; a brick border on a white kerb faces the entry lane (Street View from Calle Loira; Google view). The trees and palms are left for the detail stage. Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the Esri aerial at 0.0385 m per pixel with the long wall's north end on (-91.4, -67.8), good to about 1.5 m.

edges.note: Brick border on the kerb top (Street View from Calle Loira).

surfaces.name: Narrow planter west of the entry lane
surfaces.note: A narrow bed about 5 m long with a brick-edged white kerb and bougainvillea, its south tip just north of the entry barrier's bollard (Street View from Calle Loira, IMG_3131's white kerb nose; Google view). The white pillar with notices at its south end and the planting are left for the detail stage. Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the Esri aerial at 0.0385 m per pixel with the long wall's north end on (-91.4, -67.8), good to about 1.5 m.

edges.note: White kerb with a brick edge about 0.25 m on the asphalt (Street View from Calle Loira, IMG_3131); the bed stands at its top.

surfaces.name: Lawn strip west of the entry lane, with the CALLE DE PICASSO plinth
surfaces.note: The narrow lawn between the brick path and the house gardens, with the white CALLE DE PICASSO plinth on it (IMG_3131). Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the aerial, about 1.5 m. It is cut short at the car-park outline's north edge, which overlies the rest (discrepancy picasso-car-park-west-edge-gardens).

surfaces.name: Terracotta path between the entry lane and the lawn strip
surfaces.note: Terracotta tiles with a brick edge along the asphalt (IMG_3131); the photo shows octagon-pattern tiles, drawn here like the Juan Gris paving it joins at the north end. Traced from Dave's Google 3D top-down screenshot (Imagery © Google 2026) registered to the aerial, about 1.5 m.

edges.note: Brick edge between the path and the asphalt (IMG_3131).

surfaces.name: Kerbed pavement along the utility row, west side of Calle Pintor Picasso south of the car park

edges.note: Stone kerb about 0.12 m on the asphalt along the road side (IMG_3123, IMG_3124, IMG_3105, IMG_3106); its height is judged.

surfaces.note: Between the utility row's faces (data/picasso_service_frontage.json) and the road's mapped west edge, from the long wall's south end to the north corner of registry part 6364501UF1366S_part1. IMG_3124 shows the kerb closing in on the bin store's street door and the pavement ending at the wall foot, which is where the mapped road edge meets the wall's line; IMG_3123 and IMG_3105 show it about 1 m wide at the substation and running in to the set-back wall; IMG_2345 shows a wide paved apron in front of the slatted gate. Drawn as one raised concrete apron; whether the apron at the gate is raised is not seen.

surfaces.name: Asphalt between Calle Pintor Picasso and the hotel's lower wing
surfaces.note: The road's asphalt reaches the foot of the hotel's lower wing (IMG_3104 recycling igloos on asphalt against the wall; IMG_3105, IMG_3120-3122 asphalt to the ramps and railings at the wing's foot). Between the mapped road's east edge and the wing's registry face (6465301UF1366N_part3) up to registry part 6465301UF1366N_part2, 2.5-4.6 m wide. On the aerial the pale road surface runs to a dark band of railings and igloos along the red roof's edge. The model drew this as terracotta and lawn.

surfaces.name: Asphalt forecourt where Calle Pintor Picasso passes the hotel's low block and the pool building
surfaces.note: The pale road surface on the Esri aerial widens here between the hotel's low block, the pool building's north-east face and the plane-tree garden, with cars parked along its east side; IMG_3118 and IMG_3119 show asphalt across it to the buildings either side. Traced on the aerial, about 1-1.5 m; the garden's curved edge is generalised.

surfaces.name: Concrete lane between the pool building's sheds and lawn wall and the east building's terrace
surfaces.note: IMG_2613 and IMG_3067 show the lane paved wall to wall in pale concrete, with a darker strip and a drain grate at the paseo end. The 4 m street ribbon runs down its middle; this fills the rest, from the forecourt to the paseo, 0.15 m inside the shed strip's face, the lawn wall and the terrace wall, about 1 m. Drawn at the ground plan's concrete height, under the ribbon, so the two do not fight where the terrain bends.
